text:
Aisha: Heads up — customer reported gaps in traces for prefetcher-worker in prod. Root spans exist but lots of missing child spans (kv-cache, async steps). Anyone seen this pattern before? Dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/traces?service=prefetcher

Matt: Which runtime/version is this? Python worker or the new nodejs prefetcher? Also which exporter/collector are we using in prod?

Aisha: It's the Python prefetcher running on Dedicated prod pool (gpu-prefetch-2). Using otel-python v1.18.0 -> Otel collector -> Tempo.

Leo: Two quick things we've seen: sampling config differences between k8s deployments, and context loss crossing threads. Check env for OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER / OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG.

Sara: For nodejs we had AsyncLocalStorage issues where timers/worker threads dropped context unless we wrapped callbacks. Python can drop context across threadpools if the context isn't propagated. Are those async tasks using concurrent.futures or Celery?

Aisha: concurrent.futures ThreadPoolExecutor inside prefetcher handler.

Leo: That explains it. ThreadPoolExecutor needs context propagation. For otel-python you can use contextvars and wrap executor with context.copy_context(). Example we shipped:
```
ctx = contextvars.copy_context()
executor.submit(lambda: ctx.run(worker_func, arg))
```

Jamie: Another angle — sampling mismatch hides children. If parent sampled false, children won't show. Can you paste output of env from the pod? quick check: `kubectl -n prod exec prefetch-0 -- printenv | grep -i OTEL`

Aisha: Got it, here's the relevant block from the canary pod env:
```
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.01
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=prefetcher
```

Matt: 0.01 in prod -> only 1% sampled. Staging had 0.05 last week. That will hide most child spans. If parent is not sampled, children won't be stored even if instrumentation runs.

Sara: Quick repro: set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on in a canary and hit the prefetch path a few times, see if the child spans appear in Tempo. If they do, it's sampling.

observability-bot: ALERT: high span drop ratio detected for service=prefetcher (now 14% child-span-missing rate). See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tracing/span-loss

Leo: If you want to avoid full always_on, try parentbased_traceidratio with a higher arg (0.05 or 0.1) and a short canary rollout. Also check collector's sampling processor — we had an extra sampler in front of tempo that capped to 0.02 once.

Aisha: Good point — collector config lives in infra repo (infra/observability/collector/prod.yaml). Can infra confirm there's no extra sampler applied?

Matt: I'll open a quick PR to bump OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG to 0.05 for a 5% canary and add an override flag. Will link PR here in 10m.

Jamie: For context loss fix, we should add a small wrapper util for ThreadPoolExecutor submit calls so we don't forget. I can draft a tiny patch in the prefetcher repo: wrap_submit = lambda ex, f, *a: ex.submit(contextvars.copy_context().run, f, *a)

Aisha: Thanks — two parallel actions: (1) infra bump sampler on canary, (2) repo change to propagate context. That should tell us whether it's sampling vs context propagation.

Matt: PR: https://github.com/redwood/prefetcher/pull/412 (bump sampler arg + canary label). Please review @Leo @Sara

Leo: Reviewing now. Also added a quick Tempo query to check a sample trace: `curl -s "https://tempo.internal/api/traces?service=prefetcher&limit=5" | jq '.[0] | .spans | length'` — if it returns small numbers that's a hint.

Sara: If you need a log query, use: `source:k8s_logs service:prefetcher "trace_id:*" | sort @timestamp desc | limit 50` — that'll show which steps emitted logs with trace ids.

Aisha: Great, thanks everyone. I'll monitor the alert and post whether the child spans reappear after the canary. :thumbsup:

observability-bot: NOTE: I've muted the noisy child-span missing alert for 30m while team investigates.

Matt: Rolling the canary now (5%). Will report back after 5m.

Aisha: If this reproduces, let's also add an alert tweak to ignore short-lived canary rollouts (maybe use count over 15m) — otherwise customers get noisy paging.

Jamie: Agreed — small tuning: require >50 missing-span events in 15m to fire urgent paging. We can do that in pager policy.

Aisha: Perfect. Thanks again, team.
